cim_eredeti: China unveils autonomous excavator robot with 540-degree 3D vision
szoveg_eredeti:
The Zoomlion excavator uses a vision-language-action model to identify objects and execute construction tasks.

Its 540-degree 3D vision system provides environmental awareness, while visual feedback enables centimeter-level placement precision.

Demonstrations included automated loading, wall construction, and pipe alignment.

Construction equipment could soon take on more complex jobs without constant operator input. Chinese machinery manufacturer Zoomlion has unveiled an AI-powered excavator that can interpret its surroundings and perform construction tasks autonomously.

The machine debuted at bauma CHINA 2026 on November 24. Live demonstrations showed it handling automated loading and other assisted construction operations. Zoomlion also presented its Z01 and Z03 humanoid robots, showcasing how the company plans to bring embodied intelligence into industrial environments.

Zoomlion’s excavation robot uses a vision-language-action (VLA) model to understand its surroundings. The system identifies objects and determines their positions, orientations, and dimensions. It then translates that information into physical movements.

This technology allows the excavator to attempt more precise construction tasks. Demonstrations included wall construction and pipe alignment. A Steelwrist hydraulic attachment works with real-time visual feedback to achieve centimeter-level placement accuracy. Such precision could help automate repetitive work that normally requires careful operator control.

The machine also features a voice-controlled cab. Operators can issue commands to check equipment status or retrieve technical information. Voice interaction also handles everyday functions, including windows, lighting, and climate controls. This gives operators another way to interact with the machinery without navigating multiple physical controls.

Several onboard systems help the excavator monitor its surroundings. A panoramic camera setup provides 360-degree visibility. Its 3D visualization system extends coverage to 540 degrees. Collision warnings and electronic geofencing add further safeguards when working around obstacles and designated boundaries.

Zoomlion wants its construction machinery and humanoid robots to share technological advances. Its Zbrain Industrial Embodied Intelligence System provides the underlying framework.

The platform transfers perception and navigation technologies between different machines. Construction equipment can improve humanoid robot capabilities. Advances in robotics can also enhance the intelligence of heavy machinery. This creates a shared development approach instead of treating each machine as an isolated robotics project.

Zoomlion’s RobotOps Intelligent Operations System supports this process. It handles data collection, model training, simulation, and validation. The platform also manages deployment and ongoing maintenance.

Industrial data provides another important foundation. Zoomlion’s industrial internet platform connects more than 1.8 million machines across over 170 countries. It contains more than five petabytes of industrial data and approximately 10,000 industrial models. These resources give the company a substantial foundation for developing and refining its industrial intelligence systems.

Zoomlion’s Z03 wheeled humanoid robot demonstrated another application of embodied intelligence. At the exhibition, it sorted randomly arranged objects with millimeter-level precision.

Its onboard intelligence combines 3D visual perception with advanced motion control. This allows the robot to handle objects with different shapes, sizes, and materials. Zoomlion has developed 10 robotic models and tested them across nearly 20 application scenarios.

Some robots already perform factory inspections and logistics sorting at Zoomlion Smart City.

The company’s Z01 bipedal humanoid robot also demonstrated its service capabilities. Zoomlion plans to begin mass production soon. At the exhibition, the robot showcased coordinated movement, visitor reception, and guided tours.

cim: Önállóan építkező, AI-vezérelt kotrógépet mutatott be a Zoomlion
lead: A kínai Zoomlion 540 fokos 3D látórendszerrel és VLA-modellel szerelte fel az autonóm munkagépét, amely centiméteres pontossággal illeszt csöveket.
osszefoglalo:
A kínai Zoomlion a bauma CHINA rendezvényen mutatta be **mesterséges intelligenciával működő autonóm kotrógépét**. A munkagép egy vision-language-action (VLA) modellt használ a környezet beazonosítására, amellyel automatikusan felismeri a tárgyak helyzetét és méretét, majd ezek alapján hajtja végre a fizikai mozdulatokat.

A gép 540 fokos 3D visualizációs rendszert és valós idejű vizuális visszacsatolást kapott, ami **centiméteres pontosságú elhelyezést** tesz lehetővé a falazási és csőillesztési feladatoknál. A fülke emellett hangvezérléssel is működik, így a kezelő szóban is lekérdezheti a gép állapotát, vagy irányíthatja a klímát és a világítást.

A fejlesztést a cég Zbrain nevű rendszere hajtja, amely közös alapot biztosít a nehézgépek és a humanoid robotok számára. A vállalat saját ipari adatplatformja több mint 1,8 millió csatlakoztatott munkagép adatát használja a modellek folyamatos finomításához.
miert_szamit: Az építőipari és nehézipari vállalkozások számára a fejlesztés megmutatja, hogy a fizikai AI a **szakképzett munkaerő hiányának kiváltására** és a monoton, nagy precizitást igénylő folyamatok automatizálására is használható.
